TON is an on-delay: output Q turns on after input IN has been TRUE for the preset time PT. TOF is an off-delay: Q stays on for PT after IN goes FALSE. TP makes a fixed-length pulse when IN rises.

ET shows the elapsed time. Timers are function blocks, so each needs its own instance.
lessons.x: A TON starts the conveyor 3 seconds after the warning horn begins.
lessons.ex: Write down what a TOF with PT of 5 seconds does to a fan after the machine stops.

lessons.c:
CTU counts up on each rising edge of CU and sets Q when the count value CV reaches the preset PV. CTD counts down on each edge of CD and sets Q when CV reaches zero or below.

RESET clears a CTU. A CTD is filled with PV using its LOAD input.

lessons.c: Timers solve real problems. A debounce ignores short flickers. A timeout raises an alarm when something takes too long. Two timers can flash a lamp. A start-up delay keeps loads from starting together.
lessons.x: A sensor must stay on for 200 ms before it counts, which ignores vibration.
lessons.ex: Design a timeout alarm for a pump that runs 60 seconds without the level changing.
